query: Commission a new 24 kV outdoor circuit-breaker on a substation feeder. Verify it can interrupt the maximum three-phase fault current at its terminals and withstand the resulting recovery voltage before the feeder is energised.
answer:
## Engineering Standards Analysis — 24 kV Outdoor Circuit-Breaker Commissioning

**SOW restated:** Prove a new 24 kV outdoor feeder circuit-breaker can (a) break the maximum three-phase fault current at its own terminals and (b) withstand the recovery voltage that follows interruption, before energising.

### Governing standard
**[iec-56] — IEC 56, *High-voltage AC circuit-breakers* (4th ed., 1987)** is the controlling specification. Its scope covers HV AC breakers above 1000 V for indoor/outdoor installation, making/carrying/breaking normal and short-circuit currents [iec-56] — i.e. exactly this device and duty. The graphical symbol for the device on the single-line/schematic is **[07-13-05] "Circuit breaker"** (IEC 60617-7 §13), and IEC 56 is the behavioural standard behind that symbol [circuit-breaker][07-13-05].

### What the device must be — the relevant ratings
| Requirement in SOW | Governing rated characteristic | Why it applies |
|---|---|---|
| "24 kV" | **[rated-voltage]** Uᵣ (4.1) | Highest phase-to-phase service voltage; 24 kV is a standard Series I value. It fixes the power-frequency recovery voltage, the insulation level, and the TRV/breaking-current reference conditions [rated-voltage]. |
| "interrupt the maximum three-phase fault current at its terminals" | **[rated-short-circuit-breaking-current]** (4.101) | Highest short-circuit current breakable at Uᵣ; for a three-pole breaker its a.c. component **is** the three-phase terminal-fault current, chosen from the R10 series (…16, 20, 25, 31.5, 40 kA…). The specified maximum fault current must be ≤ this rating [rated-short-circuit-breaking-current]. |
| "withstand the resulting recovery voltage" | **[recovery-voltage]** + **[transient-recovery-voltage]** (4.102) | Recovery voltage appears across the pole after current zero [recovery-voltage]; at 24 kV (< 100 kV) the **two-parameter (u_c, t₃)** TRV envelope from Table IIA (first-pole-to-clear factor 1.5) applies, and ITRV may be neglected below 100 kV/25 kA [transient-recovery-voltage]. The prospective TRV of the circuit must lie within this rated envelope. |
| Closing onto a fault | **[rated-short-circuit-making-current]** (4.103) | A commissioned feeder breaker may close onto an existing fault; peak make = 2.5 × a.c. rms (50 Hz) and equals the peak withstand current [rated-short-circuit-making-current]. |
| "Outdoor" | **[external-insulation]** (3.101.20) → **[rated-insulation-level]** (4.2) | Outdoor service stresses the external (air/surface) insulation with pollution/humidity; it is self-restoring and, with the internal insulation, is verified by the rated impulse + power-frequency withstand of Table I (≤ 72.5 kV) [external-insulation][rated-insulation-level]. |

The fault current to compare against the rating is the circuit's **[prospective-current]** — the current that would flow with the breaker replaced by zero impedance [prospective-current].

### How "verify" is demonstrated — the applicable tests
The proof of (a)+(b) is the **short-circuit making and breaking type test** [short-circuit-test][type-test]:

- **[making-and-breaking-capacity] / [short-circuit-test]** (6.102): deemed proved by making and breaking the specified currents from 10 %→100 % of rating at rated voltage, **preferably in a three-phase circuit** for a three-pole breaker — directly matching the "three-phase fault" requirement [short-circuit-test][making-and-breaking-capacity].
- **[test-duty]** (6.106): the five standard duties; **Test-duty No. 4 = 100 % breaking + 100 % making at the full [rated-operating-sequence]** is the duty that demonstrates the maximum-fault claim (No. 5 adds full asymmetrical d.c. if opening time < 80 ms) [test-duty].
- **[short-circuit-test-quantities]** (6.104): each duty is run with the **prospective TRV envelope and the power-frequency recovery voltage (U/√3 × pole factor, held ≥ 0.1 s)** applied — this is the mechanism that verifies recovery-voltage withstand [short-circuit-test-quantities].
- **[short-circuit-test-procedure]** (6.105) and **[rated-operating-sequence]** (4.104, e.g. O-3min-CO-3min-CO) set the O/CO timing [short-circuit-test-procedure][rated-operating-sequence].
- **[single-phase-short-circuit-test]** (6.108): an *additional* duty for three-pole earthed-neutral breakers, checking unbalanced-force behaviour — relevant if this feeder breaker serves an earthed-neutral system [single-phase-short-circuit-test].

### Notable scoping calls (what does NOT apply)
- **[short-line-fault]** tests are **not required**: SLF applies only at Uᵣ ≥ 52 kV with breaking current > 12.5 kA [short-line-fault]. At 24 kV the **terminal fault** is the governing breaking duty — consistent with the SOW's "at its terminals."
- **Type vs. field commissioning:** IEC 56's making/breaking proof is a **[type-test]** on a representative breaker, not an on-site test [type-test]. So "verify before energising" is satisfied by confirming the unit's *type-test certificate* covers Uᵣ ≥ 24 kV, the rated short-circuit breaking current ≥ the calculated maximum prospective three-phase fault current at the terminals, and the rated TRV envelope ≥ the feeder's prospective TRV. The on-site commissioning step is checking nameplate ratings and dielectric/mechanical condition against these type-tested values — IEC 56 does not define an on-site fault-interruption test.

**Bottom line:** Confirm, from the breaker's IEC 56 type-test record, that Uᵣ ≥ 24 kV, rated short-circuit breaking current ≥ site maximum three-phase terminal fault, and rated (two-parameter) TRV ≥ prospective TRV at 24 kV, with the outdoor rated insulation level met. Terminal-fault Test-duty 4 (and 5 if fast-opening) is the verifying duty; short-line-fault testing is out of scope at this voltage.

query: Specify a 36 kV circuit-breaker dedicated to switching a shunt capacitor bank and energising no-load overhead lines, such that no switching overvoltages arise from restrikes.
answer:
## Engineering Standards Analysis — 36 kV restrike-free capacitive-switching circuit-breaker

**The device.** A circuit-breaker — a mechanical switching device that makes, carries and breaks both normal and abnormal (short-circuit) currents [circuit-breaker]. In IEC 60617 it is drawn as symbol **[07-13-05]** "Circuit breaker / Disjoncteur," in section [60617-7-13-switchgear-and-controlgear] of part [60617-7]. The physical device that this symbol represents is specified by **[iec-56]** (High-voltage AC circuit-breakers, 4th ed. 1987) — that is the governing specification standard here.

**The core requirement = restrike-free.** The SOW's "no switching overvoltages from restrikes" maps onto a defined performance class: a **restrike-free circuit-breaker** [restrike-free-circuit-breaker], one that "interrupts without restrike during the capacitive current-breaking test duties" ([iec-56] 3.102.12). Note the precise definitions:
- A **restrike** is current resuming **a quarter-cycle or more after current zero** ([iec-56] 3.105.47) [restrike].
- A **reignition** is current resuming **less than a quarter-cycle after** current zero ([iec-56] 3.105.46) [reignition] — far less onerous and *not* what the SOW prohibits.
So the specification must call out the **restrike** boundary explicitly; reignitions are not excluded by "restrike-free."

**Why it matters (the mechanism).** When a capacitive current (line, cable, or capacitor bank) is interrupted, trapped charge holds the load side near peak voltage, so a one-cosine **recovery voltage** builds across the open gap up to ~2× peak [recovery-voltage] (with its transient component, the TRV [transient-recovery-voltage]). A late dielectric failure — a restrike — then injects energy that escalates the overvoltage. This is precisely the hazard the SOW guards against, and it is a **breaking/de-energising** phenomenon. (The SOW says "energising," but restrikes arise on *opening* the no-load line/bank, not on closing; energising is instead a *making*/inrush duty — see inrush current below.)

**Rated characteristics to specify at 36 kV:**

| Duty in the SOW | Rated characteristic | Applies at 36 kV? |
|---|---|---|
| System voltage | **Rated voltage** U_r = 36 kV ([iec-56] 4.1) [rated-voltage] | Yes — fixes everything below |
| Dielectric withstand | **Rated insulation level**, Table I (≤72.5 kV) [rated-insulation-level] | Yes |
| Switch off one shunt bank | **Rated single capacitor bank breaking current** (4.107) [rated-single-capacitor-bank-breaking-current] | Yes (not voltage-restricted; R 10 series) |
| Switch a bank with other banks on source side | **Rated back-to-back capacitor bank breaking current** (4.110) [rated-back-to-back-capacitor-bank-breaking-current] | Yes, if back-to-back arrangement |
| Energise a bank (inrush) | **Rated capacitor bank inrush making current** (4.111) [rated-capacitor-bank-inrush-making-current] | **Mandatory** if a back-to-back rating is assigned; 2–5 kHz inrush |
| De-energise no-load overhead line | **Rated line-charging breaking current** (4.107) [rated-line-charging-breaking-current] | **See gap below** |

For every capacitive breaking duty the breaker must stay within the **maximum permissible switching overvoltages** the manufacturer declares (Table IX, columns B) [rated-single-capacitor-bank-breaking-current].

**⚠ Key gap at 36 kV — the overhead-line duty.** IEC 56 confines the **rated line-charging breaking current to three-pole breakers at rated voltage ≥ 72.5 kV** [rated-line-charging-breaking-current], and the test clause states line-charging tests below 72.5 kV are "generally unnecessary" [capacitive-current-switching-test]. At **36 kV there is no standardized Table VII line-charging value** — so the no-load-line de-energising duty cannot simply be taken from the standard; it must be handled by **special agreement** with the manufacturer (with a declared current and overvoltage limit). For context, cable-charging breaking current is "unnecessary at ≤24 kV" [rated-cable-charging-breaking-current], so at 36 kV a cable-charging rating *could* be specified if cables were in scope — but the SOW is overhead lines, not cables.

**Verification.** Restrike-free performance is proven by the **capacitive current switching test** ([iec-56] 6.111) [capacitive-current-switching-test]: four test-duty series (Table XIX) at 20–40% and ≥100% of rated capacitive current, 10 three-phase (or 12 single-phase) operations each; **acceptance requires no restrikes** and the trapped-charge voltage held 0.3 s. Critically, "laboratory verification of the line-charging breaking current is valid only if the breaker is restrike-free" (6.111.2) — i.e. the rating itself is contingent on the no-restrike behaviour the SOW demands. The short-circuit making/breaking capacity [making-and-breaking-capacity] remains a baseline type-test for any breaker but is secondary to this capacitive scope.

**Technology note.** "Restrike-free" is a *performance class, not a construction type* — any medium can qualify if it passes 6.111 [restrike-free-circuit-breaker]. At 36 kV (medium voltage), the **vacuum circuit-breaker** [vacuum-circuit-breaker] is the dominant choice; an **SF6 circuit-breaker** [sf6-circuit-breaker] is the main alternative. Both give rapid dielectric recovery favourable to restrike-free capacitive switching — but the qualification is the *test*, not the medium, so the spec should require demonstrated restrike-free performance per [iec-56] 6.111 regardless of technology.

**Bottom line for the spec.** Specify: U_r = 36 kV with the Table I insulation level; the **restrike-free** classification ([iec-56] 3.102.12); a **single (and, if applicable, back-to-back) capacitor-bank breaking current** plus the **mandatory inrush making current**, each within declared max switching overvoltages; the **no-load-line breaking duty by special agreement** (no standard value exists below 72.5 kV); and proof via the **capacitive current switching test** (6.111) with the no-restrike acceptance criterion.

query: Overhaul a flameproof (Ex d) 3.3 kV induction motor: rewind the stator, recondition the sleeve bearings, and return it to its certified condition for the hazardous area.
answer:
## Standards & clause analysis — Ex d 3.3 kV induction motor overhaul

**Governing standard.** This is a repair/overhaul of explosion-protected apparatus, so the controlling document is **IEC 79-19** *Repair and overhaul* [iec-79-19] — not the 60617 symbol parts (those only supply the diagram symbols). The whole job must be done *without invalidating the explosion-protection certification* [iec-79-19][overhaul]. Because the machine is **flameproof "d"**, every requirement comes from **IEC 79-19 clause 3** [type-of-protection-d]. The three named work scopes map to specific sub-clauses below. (The work itself is an *overhaul*/*repair*/*reclamation* — restoring the original design — and must stay clear of *modification*, which would change the certified design [overhaul][repair][reclamation][modification].)

### 1. Rewind the stator
- **Winding data & method** — obtain original winding data, preferably from the [manufacturer]; otherwise use **copy-winding** to reproduce the original exactly [copy-winding][windings] (clause 3.2.6). Copy-winding is the defined process of replacing a winding by copying the original [copy-winding].
- **Insulation** — use the same or a superior insulation class (e.g. class E → F per IEC 85), but **a superior class does NOT permit any rating increase without manufacturer reference** [insulation] (3.2.4).
- **Rotor/core** — if the stator core is skimmed or damaged it must pass a **flux (loop) test** for hot spots that could breach the temperature class; air-gap changes must not alter pressure-piling or raise external surface temperature [rotors-and-stators] (3.3.4). Faulty die-cast cages → new manufacturer rotor; bar-wound cages may be rewound to identical spec [windings] (3.2.6.2).
- **Post-rewind testing** [testing-after-repair] (3.2.6.3): winding-resistance balance, insulation-resistance (≥500 V d.c.), high-voltage test, energized rated-voltage check, plus for rotating machines a **full-speed run** (noise/vibration) and a **locked-rotor reduced-voltage full-load test** (per IEC 34). ⚠️ At **3.3 kV this is a high-voltage machine, so further/additional tests are expressly anticipated** beyond the baseline regime [testing-after-repair].

### 2. Recondition the sleeve bearings
- Plain (sleeve) bearing surfaces may be **reclaimed by electroplating or metal spraying** [sleeve-bearings] (3.3.3).
- ⚠️ Critical "d" interaction: bearing **housings often form part of the flameproof path**. Shafts and bearing housings may be reclaimed by metal spraying/sleeving (welding with care), but **any subsequent machining must be to the flamepath dimensions specified in the standard/certification** [shafts-and-housings] (3.3.2). Do not relieve the flame gap during bearing/journal reclamation.

### 3. Return to certified (flameproof) condition
- **Flameproof joints/enclosure** — prefer new manufacturer parts; on re-assembly the flameproof joints must comply with the standard/certification; reclaimed enclosure parts may be reused only if they pass the **over-pressure test** [enclosures] (3.2.1, 3.3.1).
- **Joint faces & threaded holes** — corroded flameproof joint faces may be machined only after manufacturer consultation and only if joint gap, flange dimensions and surface finish stay within limits; damaged fastener threads reclaimed only with manufacturer consultation [threaded-holes-for-fasteners] (3.3.1.2–3).
- **Terminations** — maintain creepage/clearance; a termination assembly containing a flameproof joint **shall not be modified** [terminations] (3.2.3, 3.4.3). Internal connections at least equivalent to original [internal-wiring] (3.2.5).
- **Certification governance** — check the certificate; an **"X" suffix means special conditions of use** that must be studied before repair [certificate-references][certification]. Restoring to a **serviceable condition** without prejudice to explosion-protection is the defined target [serviceable-condition]. Responsibilities: the **user** specifies the work and verifies protection on return; a competent **repairer** (with the required training/docs/facilities) does it; the **manufacturer** is the reference for winding data, spares and any rating change [user][repairer][manufacturer].

### Cross-cutting compliance flags
- **No rating/rerating creep**: rewinding for a different voltage or speed is a change requiring manufacturer reference (magnetic loading, current densities, losses, creepage/clearance, temperature class, updated rating plate) — that is the boundary between repair and **modification** [windings][modification] (3.4.4).
- If the motor is **dual-certified "d e"** (common for HV motors, terminal box in "e"), the winding rules tighten: under increased safety "e" the rewind may have to be done by the **original manufacturer** and full original winding data obtained first [type-of-protection-e][windings] (6.2.6.1) — confirm the nameplate marking.
- IEC 79-19 cross-refers to **IEC 34** (rotating machines), **IEC 85** (insulation classes), **IEC 529** (IP), **IEC 364**, and the type standard **IEC 79-1** ("d") [iec-79-19].

### Relevant 60617 symbols (for drawings/records)
- [06-08-01] induction motor, three-phase, squirrel cage · [06-04-01] machine, general (asterisk → "M") · [06-02-07] three-phase star winding · [02-01-04] enclosure/envelope outline (flameproof housing).

**Bottom line:** treat the job as an IEC 79-19 clause-3 "d" overhaul — copy-wind to original data with equal/superior insulation (no rating increase), flux-test the core, reclaim bearings/housings without violating flamepath dimensions, restore flameproof joints to certified gaps, run the full HV post-repair test set, and keep everything within the existing certificate (heed any "X").

query: In one enclosure, repair both an increased-safety (Ex e) terminal box and an intrinsically-safe (Ex i) instrument circuit, and restore both to their certified condition.
answer:
## Engineering Standards Analysis — Repair of an Ex e terminal box + Ex i instrument circuit in one enclosure

### Governing standard
The whole SOW falls under **IEC 79-19** — *Repair and overhaul of electrical apparatus for explosive gas atmospheres* [iec-79-19]. It is a procedure/requirements standard, organised as a **matrix of protection-type clause × component**. The two protection types named map to two clauses you must satisfy **simultaneously**:
- **Increased safety "e"** → defined 2.2.17; repair rules in **clause 6** [type-of-protection-e]
- **Intrinsic safety "i"** → defined 2.2.15; repair rules in **clause 4** [type-of-protection-i]

"Repair…and restore to certified condition" invokes the definitions **[repair]** (restore a damaged/worn item to a serviceable condition) and **[serviceable-condition]** (usable *without prejudice to the explosion-protection aspects, with due regard to certification*). If the work were more than fault-driven it would be **[overhaul]**; either way the certification must survive. Any change to material/fit/form/function is instead a **[modification]** (cl. 6.4 / 4.4) and needs the manufacturer or certifying authority — it is *not* covered by a "restore to certified" SOW.

### The crux: two protection types in ONE enclosure
Because Ex e (non-intrinsically-safe) and Ex i (intrinsically-safe) coexist in a single enclosure, the binding constraint is **segregation between the IS and non-IS systems**. IEC 79-19 enforces this through:
- **Terminations "i" (4.2.3):** replacements must keep creepage (per CTI)/clearance for max voltage **plus the separation needed to avoid inadvertent cross-connection** [terminations].
- **Internal wiring "i" (4.2.12):** inter-conductor distances and segregation are *critical* — disturbed wiring must be returned to its **original position**, and any damaged insulation/screens/sheaths/double-insulation replaced by equivalent material and re-fixed in the same configuration [internal-wiring].
- **The 50 mm IS/non-IS spacing** (4.2.14) that protects barriers must not be encroached by the Ex e wiring [encapsulated-parts].

So the Ex e repair must not compromise the Ex i separation, and vice-versa. Where a feature is shared (enclosure, entries), the **more demanding** requirement governs.

### Ex e terminal box — apply clause 6
| Component | Requirement (IEC 79-19) | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Enclosure (6.2.1) | Preserve the **degree of protection (IP) and temperature class shown on the certification label**; impact-test withstand maintained | [enclosures] |
| Cable/conduit entries (6.2.2) | Restore to **minimum IP54 per IEC 529**; no extra entries without the manufacturer | [cable-and-conduit-entries] |
| Terminations (6.2.3) | Materials, **creepage/clearance and CTI** are in the cert documents → replacement terminals from the manufacturer or on his advice; loose-lead terminations per cert docs | [terminations] |
| Internal connections (6.2.5) | If renewed, insulation **not electrically/thermally/mechanically inferior** and **cross-section not smaller** than original | [internal-wiring] |
| Winding insulation (6.2.4), if any | Insulation system/varnish per cert docs; otherwise seek full data from manufacturer | [insulation] |

### Ex i instrument circuit — apply clause 4
| Component | Requirement (IEC 79-19) | Page |
|---|---|---|
| Internal wiring (4.2.12) | Critical inter-conductor distances/segregation → restore to original position/configuration | [internal-wiring] |
| Terminations (4.2.3) | Same type where possible; creepage(CTI)/clearance + anti-cross-connection separation | [terminations] |
| Enclosure / entries (4.2.1, 4.2.2) | Where IP is relied on, repair must **not reduce the degree of protection** | [enclosures], [cable-and-conduit-entries] |
| Shunt-diode safety barriers / encapsulated parts (4.2.7, 4.2.14) | **Totally encapsulated — no repair**; replace only with same safety description, U value and 50 mm separation | [encapsulated-parts] |
| Optocouplers (4.2.9) | Replace only with same or directly equivalent type **and certification** | [optocouplers] |
| Transformers (4.2.13) | Replacement from the equipment manufacturer; **never** repair/replace an embedded thermal trip in the field | [transformers] |
| Non-electrical parts (4.2.15) | Fittings/windows not affecting the circuit or creepage may be replaced by equivalent new parts | [non-electrical-parts] |
| **Test after repair (4.2.16)** | Before re-installing in the hazardous area, apply **500 V a.c. for 1 min between the IS terminals and the enclosure** (may be omitted only for an insulating enclosure with one side galvanically bonded) | [testing-after-repair] |

### Process & responsibilities (clause 2)
- **[user]** selects a competent repairer and must supply the work instructions, the original **[certification]** and any special conditions of use; satisfies itself on return that protection is intact.
- **[repairer]** must hold the training, documentation and facilities (cl. 2.6); may be the user, the **[manufacturer]** or a third party.
- **[certificate-references]:** a certificate number with an **"X" suffix** means special conditions of use — the cert documents *must* be studied before this repair proceeds.
- Distinguish from **[maintenance]** (preventive, non-faulty) and from **[modification]** (design change — out of scope of "restore to certified").

### Relevant 60617 symbols (for the repair drawings/diagrams)
- **Enclosure / envelope** — [02-01-04] (a note may flag special protective features)
- **Terminal** — [03-02-02]

### Do **not** attempt to repair (replace as certified units)
Shunt-diode barriers and other encapsulated assemblies [encapsulated-parts], optocouplers [optocouplers], and IS transformers / their embedded thermal trips [transformers].

---

**Bottom line:** treat this as one job governed by IEC 79-19 but satisfying **both clause 6 (Ex e) and clause 4 (Ex i)** at once — preserve the labelled IP/temperature class and ≥IP54 entries for the Ex e box, preserve IS creepage/clearance, conductor separation and the 50 mm IS/non-IS spacing for the Ex i circuit, use only certified replacement parts/barriers, finish with the 500 V/1-min IS-to-earth test, and keep everything within the existing certificate (study it first if it carries an "X").

query: Document a new 11 kV outgoing feeder bay comprising an isolator, a circuit-breaker, a current transformer and a voltmeter. The circuit-breaker must be rated for the busbar fault level.
answer:
I have enough to synthesize. Here is the analysis.

---

# SOW Analysis — 11 kV Outgoing Feeder Bay

**Scope:** isolator + circuit-breaker + current transformer + voltmeter, with the circuit-breaker rated for the busbar fault level. Below, each item is mapped to its IEC 60617 graphical symbol, and the circuit-breaker's rating requirement is mapped to the governing specification standard (IEC 56) and its clauses.

## 1. Symbols to use on the diagram (IEC 60617)

| Bay item | Symbol | Name | Source |
|----------|--------|------|--------|
| Isolator | **[07-13-06]** | Disconnector (isolator) — *Sectionneur* | Part 7, §13 [60617-7-13-switchgear-and-controlgear] |
| Circuit-breaker | **[07-13-05]** | Circuit breaker — *Disjoncteur* | Part 7, §13 [60617-7-13-switchgear-and-controlgear] |
| Current transformer | **[06-09-10]** / **[06-09-11]** | Current transformer (general symbol, Form 1 / Form 2) | Part 6, §09 |
| Voltmeter | **[08-02-01]** | Voltmeter — *Voltmètre* | Part 8, §02 |

Notes on selection:
- **Isolator vs. switch-disconnector.** [07-13-06] is the plain off-load disconnector. If the bay device is intended to break load current, the correct symbol is instead the switch-disconnector [07-13-08]; for a maintenance-earthing/locking variant, [07-13-10]. The SOW says "isolator", so [07-13-06] is the literal match [60617-7-13-switchgear-and-controlgear].
- **Current transformer.** [06-09-10]/[06-09-11] are the general-purpose CT symbols. If the CT is drawn with detailed cores/windings (e.g. metering + protection cores), use a worked example from Part 6 §13 — e.g. two secondary windings on one core [06-13-04]/[06-13-05] [60617-6-13-examples-of-measuring-transformers].
- **Voltmeter measurement chain.** A voltmeter [08-02-01] cannot connect directly to an 11 kV bus; it is fed through a **voltage transformer [06-13-01]** (listed in [60617-6-13-examples-of-measuring-transformers]). If the SOW's intent is bus voltage indication, the diagram will normally also show a VT. ([08-02-11] is the *differential* voltmeter — only if a difference measurement is intended.)

## 2. The circuit-breaker rating — applicable standard & clauses

The graphical symbol carries no rating; the requirement *"rated for the busbar fault level"* is governed by **IEC 56 — High-voltage AC circuit-breakers** (4th ed., 1987), which is the specification standard behind symbol [07-13-05] [circuit-breaker] [iec-56]. The relevant rated characteristics:

- **Busbar fault level → rated short-circuit breaking current (IEC 56 cl. 4.101).** The "fault level" is the **prospective current** the busbar can deliver (the current with the breaker replaced by zero impedance) [prospective-current]. The breaker must be selected so its **rated short-circuit breaking current** (r.m.s. a.c. component, from the R10 series … 16, 20, 25, **31.5**, 40 kA …) is ≥ the calculated busbar fault current at 11 kV [rated-short-circuit-breaking-current].
- **Making duty (cl. 4.103).** It must also close onto a fault: the **rated short-circuit making current** = 2.5× (50 Hz) the breaking-current a.c. component [rated-short-circuit-making-current].
- **Withstand while carrying the fault (cl. 4.5 / 4.6).** Equal-by-definition to the breaking current and making current respectively: **rated short-time withstand current** (thermal, carried for the rated duration of short-circuit) [rated-short-time-withstand-current] and **rated peak withstand current** (electrodynamic peak) [rated-peak-withstand-current]. These bound the fault the closed breaker survives before clearing.
- **Voltage class (cl. 4.1 / 4.2).** "11 kV" fixes the **rated voltage U_r** (highest phase-to-phase r.m.s. — the standard class is 12 kV) [rated-voltage] and the coordinated **rated insulation level** (Table I, ≤ 72.5 kV) [rated-insulation-level].
- **Continuous load (cl. 4.4).** Separately size the **rated normal current** (R10 series 400/630/800/1250 A …) to the feeder's continuous load — independent of fault level [rated-normal-current].

**Bottom line:** specify the breaker as (≈12 kV, U_r) / (rated normal current = feeder load) / (rated short-circuit breaking current ≥ busbar fault level, R10 value), and the short-time/peak withstand and making current follow by IEC 56's defined equalities.

## 3. Caveats / coverage gaps
- IEC 56 governs **only the circuit-breaker**. The **isolator** and **current transformer** must independently withstand the same busbar fault (their own short-time/peak withstand ratings) — but their specification standards (IEC 62271-102 for disconnectors, IEC 61869-2 for CTs) are **not present in this wiki**, so only the symbol-level guidance above is sourced here.
- All symbols cited are from the 1983 1st-edition parts (617-x), the editions held in the collection.

query: What is the difference between a circuit-breaker and a disconnector, and which IEC standard specifies the ratings and tests for the circuit-breaker?
answer:
## Circuit-breaker vs. disconnector

These are two distinct **mechanical switching devices**, sitting side-by-side in the same IEC 60617-7 "Switchgear and controlgear" section [60617-7-13-switchgear-and-controlgear].

**Circuit-breaker** — symbol **[07-13-05]** (FR *Disjoncteur*). A circuit-breaker is a switching device capable of **making, carrying and breaking currents under normal conditions, and also making, carrying for a specified time, and breaking currents under abnormal conditions such as short-circuit** [circuit-breaker] ([iec-56] 3.102.3 / IEV 441-14-20). What sets it apart from a plain switch is precisely its **short-circuit interrupting duty** — it is built to interrupt fault currents, with a continuous-current [main-contact] and an [arcing-contact] that takes the arc during interruption.

**Disconnector (isolator)** — symbol **[07-13-06]** (FR *Sectionneur*). A disconnector is an **isolating device**: its job is to provide a visible/positive isolating gap in the circuit for safety, not to interrupt load or fault current. It is essentially an **off-load** device. The contrast is made explicit by the neighbouring symbols in the same table: the **switch-disconnector** [07-13-08] is labelled the "on-load isolating switch" (FR *Interrupteur-sectionneur*), i.e. you need that variant to break load current — the plain disconnector does not [60617-7-13-switchgear-and-controlgear]. The section also offers a two-way disconnector with centre-off isolating position [07-13-07] and a manually-operated disconnector with blocking device [07-13-10].

**In short:** the circuit-breaker is the active protective device that interrupts normal *and* short-circuit currents; the disconnector is a passive isolating device that establishes a safe open gap and is operated essentially without load.

## Which standard specifies the circuit-breaker's ratings and tests

**IEC 56 — "High-voltage alternating-current circuit-breakers"** (4th edition, 1987) [iec-56]. It is a *specification* standard (not a symbol dictionary) defining the ratings, design requirements and tests for HV AC circuit-breakers on systems above 1000 V; the device represented by symbol [07-13-05] is exactly the circuit-breaker specified by IEC 56 [iec-56].

- **Ratings → clause 4.** The rated characteristics are the values the breaker is designed and guaranteed to meet — rated voltage [rated-voltage], rated insulation level [rated-insulation-level], rated frequency, rated normal current, rated short-time and peak withstand currents, rated short-circuit breaking and making currents, rated transient recovery voltage, and rated operating sequence [rated-value] ([iec-56] clause 4).
- **Tests → clause 6 (type tests).** These verify a representative breaker meets its ratings: dielectric tests (6.1), radio-interference-voltage tests (6.2), temperature-rise tests (6.3), main-circuit resistance (6.4), short-time/peak withstand tests (6.5), mechanical/environmental tests (6.101), and short-circuit making-and-breaking tests including terminal-fault, short-line-fault and out-of-phase tests (6.102–6.110), plus capacitive and small-inductive switching [type-test].

(Note: the disconnector has no ratings/tests specification within this wiki — IEC 56 governs the circuit-breaker specifically.)
